title: Learning proposal
description: One item of `<ticketDir>/proposals.json` ({"schemaVersion": 1, "ticket": "<id>", "proposals": [...]}), written by the reflect node. A proposal changes nothing by itself (decision D10): only the user approves it (`sdlc learn apply --actor user`, or `sdlc learn review` at a terminal), which copies it to `.sdlc/learning/` as a lesson (lesson.schema.json). Beyond this schema the reflect gate refuses: an unknown type, scope nodes not in the graph, unknown stacks, absolute or `..` scope paths, evidence that does not resolve (decisions.jsonl line or path:line), and prose (title, body, metric, baseline) that contains commands, tool names, destinations (URL, address, IP, share) or paths outside scope.paths.

id.description: Unique within the file. Globally a proposal is <ticket>/<id>.

type.description: lesson: guidance added to packets of the scoped nodes; rule: a rulepack rule to add or change; profile: a project profile setting (e.g. a nodeOverrides tier); harness: a change to the harness itself, which the harness never applies to its own graph, gates or driver (it goes to the harness maintainers).

body.description: What to do differently, in prose. No commands, tool names, destinations or paths outside scope.

ref.description: decisions.jsonl#<line> (1-based line of the ticket's decision log, as `sdlc reflect-signals` reports it) or <path>:<line>[-<line>] in a repository or the ticket folder.

scope.description: Where it applies; packets carry an applied lesson by node, stack and path.

paths.description: Repository-relative paths or globs; empty = every path.

metric.description: What it should improve, measurably (e.g. code-review loop-backs per ticket on the scoped nodes).

baseline.description: The metric's value on this ticket (what the retro compares against).

status.description: Always `proposed` here; approval and retirement live in the lesson (lesson.schema.json).

round.description: Review round the proposal came from (0 = first delivery).
